correctness.rationale: For every \(N\), \(s_b(N)\equiv N\pmod{b-1}\), giving the necessary divisor \(g\). Multiplication by \(n/g\) permutes residues modulo \((b-1)/g\), so the first \(q=(b-1)/g\) multiples supply one digit-sum representative of every admissible residue class. The focal paper’s Theorem 4 fills the upward ray in each residue by steps of \(b-1\), proving the tail. Disjoint base-\(b\) block concatenation proves additive closure. These arguments cover \(b=2\), \(n=1\), and all gcd boundary cases without exceptions.

value.rationale: The focal literature treats minimum digit sums and one-residue progressions. The new statement determines the entire infinite tail of the attainable spectrum for every base and modulus, reducing all remaining uncertainty to finitely many small values. The numerical-semigroup formulation is a natural structural invariant: it supplies finite complement, conductor, and additive closure, and turns an infinite realization problem into a finite exceptional-set problem.
